lines.text: Nine dots in a square grid. How many circles pass through at least three of them?
lines.caption: Nine dots in a square grid. How many circles pass through at least three of them?

lines.text: Lots of kids answer seventy-six. <short pause> The real answer is much smaller!
lines.caption: Lots of kids answer seventy-six. The real answer is much smaller!

lines.text: Hello there! My name is Vantee. Let's count these circles the smart way.
lines.caption: Hello there! My name is Vantee. Let's count these circles the smart way.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Nine points are marked. Each of x and y is zero, one, or two.
lines.caption: Nine points are marked. Each of x and y is zero, one, or two.

lines.text: How many different circles pass through at least three of the marked points?
lines.caption: How many different circles pass through at least three of the marked points?

lines.text: Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices.

lines.text: What are we counting?
lines.caption: What are we counting?

lines.text: Pick any three points that are not on one line.
lines.caption: Pick any three points that are not on one line.

lines.text: Exactly one circle goes through all three of them.
lines.caption: Exactly one circle goes through all three of them.

lines.text: Three points on one line? No circle can pass through all three.
lines.caption: Three points on one line? No circle can pass through all three.

lines.text: Watch the word different. A circle through four points still counts only once.
lines.caption: Watch the word different. A circle through four points still counts only once.

lines.text: Now pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our plan: count groups of three, then fix the repeats.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our plan: count groups of three, then fix the repeats.

lines.text: How many ways can we pick three of the nine points?
lines.caption: How many ways can we pick three of the nine points?

lines.text: Nine times eight times seven, over three times two times one.
lines.caption: Nine times eight times seven, over three times two times one.

lines.text: That makes eighty-four groups of three.
lines.caption: That makes eighty-four groups of three.

lines.text: Throw out groups on one line: three rows, three columns, two diagonals. That's eight.
lines.caption: Throw out groups on one line: three rows, three columns, two diagonals. That's eight.

lines.text: Eighty-four minus eight leaves seventy-six groups.
lines.caption: Eighty-four minus eight leaves seventy-six groups.

lines.text: Is it seventy-six circles, then?
lines.caption: Is it seventy-six circles, then?

lines.text: Not so fast! Look at this little square.
lines.caption: Not so fast! Look at this little square.

lines.text: All four corners sit on one circle.
lines.caption: All four corners sit on one circle.

lines.text: Leave out any one corner. The other three give the SAME circle.
lines.caption: Leave out any one corner. The other three give the SAME circle.

lines.text: So this one circle got counted four times!
lines.caption: So this one circle got counted four times!

lines.text: So let's hunt for every circle that passes through four points.
lines.caption: So let's hunt for every circle that passes through four points.

lines.text: Any rectangle works. Its two diagonals are equal, and they cross at their middles.
lines.caption: Any rectangle works. Its two diagonals are equal, and they cross at their middles.

lines.text: That point is the same distance from all four corners: the center!
lines.caption: That point is the same distance from all four corners: the center!

lines.text: First, four small squares.
lines.caption: First, four small squares.

lines.text: Then one big square, and one tilted square.
lines.caption: Then one big square, and one tilted square.

lines.text: Next, the long rectangles. Two lie flat, and two stand up.
lines.caption: Next, the long rectangles. Two lie flat, and two stand up.

lines.text: Here's a sneaky one: a trapezoid whose two short sides match.
lines.caption: Here's a sneaky one: a trapezoid whose two short sides match.

lines.text: It's symmetric, so its center sits on the mirror line, the same distance from all four corners.
lines.caption: It's symmetric, so its center sits on the mirror line, the same distance from all four corners.

lines.text: It can face each of the four corners, so there are four trapezoids.
lines.caption: It can face each of the four corners, so there are four trapezoids.

lines.text: Six squares, four rectangles, four trapezoids. That's fourteen circles!
lines.caption: Six squares, four rectangles, four trapezoids. That's fourteen circles!

lines.text: A five-point circle would have to be one of these fourteen. None of them touches a fifth dot.
lines.caption: A five-point circle would have to be one of these fourteen. None of them touches a fifth dot.

lines.text: Each of these fourteen circles was counted four times. So remove three extra copies of each.
lines.caption: Each of these fourteen circles was counted four times. So remove three extra copies of each.

lines.text: Fourteen times three is forty-two.
lines.caption: Fourteen times three is forty-two.

lines.text: Seventy-six take away forty-two leaves thirty-four!
lines.caption: Seventy-six take away forty-two leaves thirty-four!

lines.text: The answer is thirty-four circles. That's Choice B!
lines.caption: The answer is thirty-four circles. That's Choice B!

lines.text: Here's another way. Split all seventy-six groups into two piles.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Split all seventy-six groups into two piles.

lines.text: Pile one holds every group inside a four-point circle.
lines.caption: Pile one holds every group inside a four-point circle.

lines.text: Fourteen circles times four groups is fifty-six groups, but only fourteen circles.
lines.caption: Fourteen circles times four groups is fifty-six groups, but only fourteen circles.

lines.text: Pile two holds the other twenty groups. Each one makes its very own circle.
lines.caption: Pile two holds the other twenty groups. Each one makes its very own circle.

lines.text: Let's check those twenty. They come in four families.
lines.caption: Let's check those twenty. They come in four families.

lines.text: Family one: a corner, the middle point, and the next corner. There are four.
lines.caption: Family one: a corner, the middle point, and the next corner. There are four.

lines.text: Family two: two corners on one side, plus the middle of the far side. Four again.
lines.caption: Family two: two corners on one side, plus the middle of the far side. Four again.

lines.text: Family three: one corner and two points it can reach with a knight's move. Four more.
lines.caption: Family three: one corner and two points it can reach with a knight's move. Four more.

lines.text: Family four: a corner, the middle point, and the middle of a side away from that corner.
lines.caption: Family four: a corner, the middle point, and the middle of a side away from that corner.

lines.text: These circles bulge outside the grid. There are eight of them.
lines.caption: These circles bulge outside the grid. There are eight of them.

lines.text: Four plus four plus four plus eight is twenty.
lines.caption: Four plus four plus four plus eight is twenty.

lines.text: Fourteen plus twenty is thirty-four. This way is great for double-checking!
lines.caption: Fourteen plus twenty is thirty-four. This way is great for double-checking!

lines.text: Now, let's look at the traps.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the traps.

lines.text: Seventy-six counts every group as its own circle. The repeats were never fixed.
lines.caption: Seventy-six counts every group as its own circle. The repeats were never fixed.

lines.text: Sixty-two takes away only one copy of each four-point circle. We must remove three.
lines.caption: Sixty-two takes away only one copy of each four-point circle. We must remove three.

lines.text: Forty-eight takes away two copies. That's still one too few.
lines.caption: Forty-eight takes away two copies. That's still one too few.

lines.text: Twenty misses the fourteen circles that pass through four points.
lines.caption: Twenty misses the fourteen circles that pass through four points.

lines.text: Always ask: did I count any circle more than once?
lines.caption: Always ask: did I count any circle more than once?

lines.text: Your turn! Take away the middle point. Now only eight points are left.
lines.caption: Your turn! Take away the middle point. Now only eight points are left.

lines.text: How many different circles pass through at least three of these eight points?
lines.caption: How many different circles pass through at least three of these eight points?

lines.text: Pause the video and use the same plan. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and use the same plan. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! First, count the groups of three.
lines.caption: Welcome back! First, count the groups of three.

lines.text: Eight times seven times six, over three times two times one, is fifty-six.
lines.caption: Eight times seven times six, over three times two times one, is fifty-six.

lines.text: Only the four sides are lines of three now. The diagonals lost their middle point.
lines.caption: Only the four sides are lines of three now. The diagonals lost their middle point.

lines.text: Fifty-six minus four leaves fifty-two groups.
lines.caption: Fifty-six minus four leaves fifty-two groups.

lines.text: Each small square used the middle point. So its circle now hits only three points.
lines.caption: Each small square used the middle point. So its circle now hits only three points.

lines.text: That leaves ten four-point circles: two squares, four rectangles, four trapezoids.
lines.caption: That leaves ten four-point circles: two squares, four rectangles, four trapezoids.

lines.text: Ten times three is thirty extra copies. Fifty-two minus thirty is twenty-two!
lines.caption: Ten times three is thirty extra copies. Fifty-two minus thirty is twenty-two!

lines.text: The answer is twenty-two circles. Great work!
lines.caption: The answer is twenty-two circles. Great work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea.

lines.text: Three points not on a line make one circle. So count the groups of three.
lines.caption: Three points not on a line make one circle. So count the groups of three.

lines.text: Then fix the repeats. A four-point circle was counted four times, so remove three.
lines.caption: Then fix the repeats. A four-point circle was counted four times, so remove three.

lines.text: I'm Vantee, and thanks for counting circles with me!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee, and thanks for counting circles with me!
